title: Stimulated emission for a three-level artificial atom in waveguide quantum electrodynamics
authors: O. A. Chuikin, Ya. S. Greenberg, V. V. Taravkova, O. V. Kibis
abstract: This work is devoted to a theoretical study of the interaction of a quantum three-level ladder system with a continuous electromagnetic field in a one-dimensional open waveguide. We consider a situation closely resembling stimulated emission - the scattering of a single-photon exponential pulse by an excited three-level emitter. Using the real-space formalism, we obtain an analytical expression for the wavefunction of our system. We show that, for the low anharmonicity of a three-level system inherent to a transmon (the most common type of artificial atom), the influence of the third level can have a significant effect on the system's behavior. Namely, the presence of the third level largely suppresses the stimulated emission effect if the relative anharmonicity is lower than $| α_r | < 4\%$. However, for a three-level system, it is possible to obtain correlation effects such as photon bunching in the reflected field, which can also be 'switched off' by tuning the incident photon parameters.
summary: This theoretical work analyzes stimulated emission from a three-level artificial atom coupled to a waveguide. By solving the system's dynamics, the authors demonstrate that the third level strongly modifies the scattering process, suppressing emission compared to a simple two-level model. Crucially, they predict the emergence of photon bunching correlations in the reflected field, offering a diagnostic tool for characterizing the emitter's internal structure.
main_problem: The paper theoretically investigates stimulated emission—the scattering of a single-photon pulse by an excited three-level emitter (3LE) in a 1D waveguide.
main_result: The presence of the third level significantly suppresses stimulated emission for low anharmonicity (like transmons) but can induce novel correlation effects, such as photon bunching, in the reflected field.
method: The study employs the real-space formalism, solving coupled differential equations derived from the time-dependent Schrödinger equation for the system's probability amplitudes.
model_or_system: The system models a quantum three-level ladder system coupled to a one-dimensional open waveguide, closely mimicking artificial atoms like transmons.
key_observables: Probability amplitudes for the excited state ($|fangle$), single-photon amplitudes ($ eta_{R/L}$), and two-photon correlation functions ($P_{RR}, P_{LL}, P_{RL}$).
important_parameters: Low relative anharmonicity ($|\alpha_r| < 4\%$), incident pulse spectral width ($\Delta\omega$), and decay rates ($\Gamma_1, \Gamma_2$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes photon indistinguishability and is restricted to the two-excitation subspace.
figures_summary: Figures compare the spatial distribution of two-photon states for 3LE vs. TLS, showing bunching in 3LE and antibunching in TLS, and illustrate the dependence of scattering probabilities on anharmonicity and pulse width.
paper_structure: The paper develops the formalism by deriving coupled differential equations for various probability amplitudes, solves these equations for specific pulse shapes (exponential), and then analyzes the resulting probabilities to compare 3LE dynamics against the standard two-level system (TLS) benchmark.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant as it explores how higher-level structure (the third level) modifies fundamental quantum optical processes like stimulated emission and photon correlation in solid-state quantum emitters.
